rule: Sharing a map, target class, equipment requirement or extraction condition is acceptable only when the player is solving a materially different operational problem. Cosmetic substitutions do not create a new quest.

conflictGroups.risk: Both use a headset and successful extraction and could collapse into the same wear-headset-and-fight template.

requiredSeparation.acoustic-discipline: Mandatory combat remains zero; the point is route reconnaissance and restraint.
requiredSeparation.acoustic-contact: A short combat application follows later; the point is choosing a contact using already-established situational awareness.

conflictGroups.mergeTrigger: If Acoustic Discipline gains a required kill condition, merge it with Acoustic Contact or redesign one of them.

conflictGroups.risk: Light armor, helmet and heavy armor can easily become an equipment-class staircase with the same kill-and-extract loop.

requiredSeparation.mobility-doctrine: Protection is deliberately light because movement is the tactical advantage.
requiredSeparation.heavy-assault: Protection is deliberately heavy because surviving a prepared assault position justifies accepting the mobility cost; head protection is folded into this operation rather than spun out into another quest.

conflictGroups.mergeTrigger: If the heavy operation cannot obtain a materially different assault context, retain only Mobility Doctrine rather than publish a class-upgrade sequel.

conflictGroups.risk: Two long-range quests differ only by distance wording or target count.

requiredSeparation.observation-window: Owns the complete precision theme: obtain stand-off control, solve one selected threat problem and disengage before the position becomes predictable.

conflictGroups.mergeTrigger: Already executed: Precision Denial remains merged unless a future concept introduces a genuinely different player decision that cannot fit Observation Window.

conflictGroups.risk: All three can look like location-bound kill-and-extract quests when stripped of context.

requiredSeparation.route-security: Ordinary Scav pressure on Customs; restore basic logistics movement.
requiredSeparation.contractor-intercept: Hostile PMC movement on Reserve; deny a specific crossing window used by trained competitors.
requiredSeparation.break-the-perimeter: Rogue defensive network on Lighthouse; disrupt a prepared fire-control perimeter rather than clear a road.

strengtheningOptions.contractor-intercept: Prefer a native SPT 4.1.5 time-window condition if exact semantics and overlap review support it; the narrative already describes a movement window. Do not add a gear restriction merely to force uniqueness.
strengtheningOptions.break-the-perimeter: Keep Water Treatment as narrative context unless an exact sub-location selector is proven. The Rogue role and Lighthouse map are the defining native constraints.

conflictGroups.mergeTrigger: If Contractor Intercept cannot preserve any meaningful window/context distinction beyond target=PMC and map=Reserve, review it against Route Security before runtime admission.

conflictGroups.risk: Two operations use Customs and could feel like repeated use of the same map without purpose.

requiredSeparation.borrowed-access: Reconnaissance/access problem: prove one restricted route is usable; combat is not the defining objective.
requiredSeparation.route-security: Later consequence: local Scavs make movement through the broader corridor unreliable and must be removed before extraction.

conflictGroups.narrativeDecision: The shared map is intentional continuity. The player first learns a route, then later helps keep the larger corridor operational. Do not create a third Customs operation in this wave without a new capability or consequence.

conflictGroups.risk: A generic cross-map survival checklist would add duration but not a new late-game decision.

requiredSeparation.internal-security: Existing Labs access is exercised under Raider pressure; entry itself is not rewarded and the player must leave after one security disruption.
requiredSeparation.endurance-circuit: Not admitted. It may return only with a distinct operational problem that native SPT 4.1.5 mechanics can represent without becoming survive-on-three-maps bookkeeping.

conflictGroups.mergeTrigger: No replacement is required if Endurance Circuit never clears the admission gate.
